model: Proline Prosonic Flow G 500 ultrasonic gas flowmeter (Modbus RS485)
applies_to: Prosonic Flow G 500 with the Modbus RS485 communication option, parameter description GP01133D/06/EN/02.24-00.
summary: Prosonic Flow G 500 is the remote-transmitter version of the Endress+Hauser ultrasonic gas flowmeter. With the Modbus RS485 option it is a Modbus RTU slave. This map covers flow, gas property and signal-quality values, totalizers, unit codes, diagnostics, serial settings and identification.

addressing.note: Registers are printed in the Modbus Application Protocol form, which the manual equates with Modicon 3XXXX/4XXXX numbers (its example: mass flow 2007 = 32007), and the scan list calls register addresses 1-based. Subtract 1 on the wire.

source.title: Description of Device Parameters Proline Prosonic Flow G 500 ultrasonic gas flowmeter
source.pages: Byte order description pp. 155-157; address model p. 231; process variables pp. 251-252; Modbus configuration p. 271

notes: Integrator subset of a parameter manual that gives a register for every menu item; display, I/O-module, sensor adjustment, web server and service parameters are left out.

Float word order follows the Byte order parameter (register 4915). The factory setting 1-0-3-2 sends byte 1, byte 0, byte 3, byte 2, where byte 3 holds sign and exponent, so floats are CDAB. Changing Byte order changes every float.
Integer parameters are 2 bytes and listed as UINT16; at 1-0-3-2 integers go out MSB first.
Unit picklists (volume, mass, temperature and so on) are long code lists; read the unit register and look the code up in the manual.
Totalizer control registers are left out because the extracted option list does not line up cleanly in the source table.

Parity codes conflict inside the manual: the parameter description lists 2 = None/1 stop bit and 3 = None/2 stop bits, while the register table lists them the other way round. The enum is left out; set parity on the device display or check by reading back.
The device also supports Modbus ASCII (Data transfer mode, register 4913); the factory setting is RTU.

integration.summary: Read the process value floats (CDAB at the factory byte order) with function 03 or 04 and check Actual diagnostics (2732). Read the unit registers once so you know the engineering unit of each value.
integration.enable: The Modbus RS485 option must be ordered. Bus address, baud rate, parity and byte order are under Expert > Communication > Modbus configuration (registers 4910-4917).
quirks: Factory byte order 1-0-3-2 gives CDAB floats; adjust the device Byte order (4915) rather than the PLC if needed.
Function 03 and 04 both read the same registers; write with 06 or 16.
setup: Check the factory bus address, baud rate and parity on the device before connecting; change them in the Modbus configuration menu.
gotchas: Avoid cyclic writes to non-volatile parameters; the EEPROM write count is limited.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
